TOP FINDING: I approve the six proposed files for root source consideration only. The executable Core JSON implementation is unchanged, the two Rustdoc insertions and the contract document accurately describe that implementation on the supplied bodies, the six final test corrections are source-derived rather than output-fitted, and root's recorded final run passed all eleven new functions. This is not integration, runtime/security adoption, backend acceptance, or a universal parser proof. Root alone selects, integrates and adopts.

SUBJECT AND PRODUCTION PRESERVATION. The proposed integration map binds: (1) crates/mori-core/src/json.rs as bodies/WHOLE_CURRENT_RUSTDOC_AFTER/json.rs, 11253 bytes, SHA256 7c59607ff6435cbb47b264ed5fca3d2b0bc35ae89a335b8ad5f356a987473b93; (2) docs/core-json-budget-contract.md, bodies/WHOLE_CURRENT_CONTRACT_DOC/core-json-budget-contract.md, 6098 bytes, SHA256 fb0614bc35a15a40f4e2bf12255a5031f0756e850b1ea8ecf0051a6f54265036; (3) final crates/mori-core/tests/core3_json_budget_coverage.rs, bodies/FINAL_COMPLETE_TEST/core3_json_budget_coverage.rs, 15713 bytes, SHA256 09fb2291395a3a0693b8e20459cda723dafdb101dcef59881057c48111836fbd; (4) unchanged corrected crates/mori-core/tests/core3_json_budget.rs, 6095 bytes, SHA256 429be19445438ac3ebe412df58780e8ebaedc5462c0f95ec0e756e6b34098dd2; (5) corrected WITNESSES.json, 4876 bytes, SHA256 14d65e1d07a9b5dd765b164f56fe3bb99b1dd1f348b093ae178c3b007ae01044; and (6) corrected EXPECTATIONS.json, 7455 bytes, SHA256 0129c592d21a390a098ff32d1e44602a9304bcd63121d68fc6f2455658199687. The executable before-Rustdoc code is bodies/C07/json.rs, 9827 bytes, SHA256 f61537bf5c1f38f9f96fb411637f76c75063da47cf94950a433f87f40bae82c8. bodies/FINAL_UNCHANGED_CODE_RUSTDOC_PROOF/PRODUCTION-COMMENT-ONLY-PROOF.json and bodies/FINAL_FULL_RUSTDOC_DIFF/PRODUCTION-RUSTDOC-ONLY.diff show exactly two triple-slash Rustdoc insertions, 22 added lines, and byte equality of every non-Rustdoc line. I therefore do not infer production correctness from comment equality; I reviewed the executable C07 semantics separately below. There is no production API, parser-behaviour, limit, feature, dependency, canonical-backend-budget or shared-compiler change in this proposal.

COUNTING AND CALLER-BUDGET SEMANTICS RECONCILED. In C07, parse_budgeted begins: 'if text.len() > budget.max_bytes { return Err(BudgetedParseError::Budget { kind: JsonBudgetKind::Bytes, limit: budget.max_bytes }); }'. For Rust &str, text.len() is UTF-8 bytes. Refusal is strictly greater, so all limits are inclusive upper bounds, and the byte check precedes Deserializer construction and decoding. BudgetSeed::deserialize performs 'let count = self.nodes.get().saturating_add(1); self.nodes.set(count); if count > self.budget.max_nodes { ... Nodes ... } if self.depth > self.budget.max_depth { ... Depth ... } d.deserialize_any(self)'. That establishes one node per value-deserialize entry, root depth 0, and Nodes before Depth at a single entry. visit_seq and visit_map build children with 'depth: self.depth + 1'. Object keys are obtained by 'a.next_key::<String>()' and are not passed through BudgetSeed; only member values are counted by next_value_seed. The Rustdoc statement 'Nodes count one per value deserialization entry: the root, every array element and every object member value; object keys are not nodes' and the contract table in the contract document match the source. The proposed Rustdoc correctly says: 'A budget is an inclusive upper bound, not a guaranteed acceptance domain.' It does not promise that text satisfying max_bytes/max_nodes/max_depth will parse. Syntax errors, duplicate decoded keys, trailing data, number/string refusals and the serde_json recursion guard remain BudgetedParseError::Json refusals. No hidden widening to guaranteed acceptance and no narrowing to the legacy 32/65536/1MiB bounds is present: parse_budgeted uses only the caller budget, while legacy parse, parse_limited and deserialize_strict retain their separate Seed bounds.

DUPLICATES, STREAMING ORDER AND TRAILING INPUT. BudgetSeed::visit_map checks 'if out.contains_key(&k) { return Err(A::Error::custom("duplicate decoded key")); }' after obtaining the decoded String key and before 'a.next_value_seed' for that member. Escaped and literal spellings that decode alike therefore collide at every nesting level, while identical keys in sibling objects do not. parse_budgeted calls 'decoder.end()' only after a successful root value, so trailing non-whitespace is refused after streaming; only space, tab, CR and LF are JSON whitespace in the pinned deserializer. The refusal order documented in both Rustdoc and contract doc is source-accurate: Bytes precheck; then document-order value entries with Nodes then Depth; duplicate decoded key when the key is read and before its value; then callee syntax/string/number/recursion errors as encountered; then trailing check. This validates the intentional retention of the extra trailing quote in the two decoded-duplicate raw inputs r#"{"\\u0061":1,"a":2}""# and r#"{"a":1,"\\u0061":2}""#: their duplicate refusal occurs during visit_map streaming, before root success and before decoder.end(), so relabelling or stripping them as trailing positives would be wrong. It also validates retaining assert_budget(r#"{"a":[{"a":1}]}""#, budget(99,99,2), Depth, 2): the depth-3 scalar entry is refused during streaming before any trailing check, so this is a genuine Depth-before-trailing witness rather than a blanket raw-quote exception requiring correction.

VALUE ROOTS, ERROR REPRESENTATION AND DISPLAY. Core parse_budgeted returns a general serde_json::Value. Scalar, array and object roots are valid; unknown object members are retained. No object-only root, deny_unknown_fields, Fields/TryFrom or backend V1-V13 rule is imported into Core. Budget refusals preserve kind and limit structurally as BudgetedParseError::Budget { kind, limit }; callers do not need string matching. BudgetedParseError's Display is 'JSON parse budget exceeded: {kind:?} limit {limit}'. Non-budget failures become Error::new("json", e.to_string()); in bodies/C02/ir.rs, Error::new prefixes the code with 'mori::core::', giving mori::core::json, and sets offset and step to None; Error Display is '{code}: {message}'. The tests' assertion strength is therefore: exact Budget enum equality for budget cases, exact Json code/offset/step, and message-meaning containment for Json text. They do not pin complete serde_json message goldens or exact line/column suffixes. bodies/SERDE_ERROR/error.rs shows the suffix ' at line L column C' is appended only when the stored line is nonzero and custom messages traverse make_error/parse_line_col. The contract document correctly tells callers to use the typed budget variant or Core code rather than string-match suffixes. That is adequate for this source consideration, but it is not exact byte-for-byte serde error-message coverage; a pinned-library suffix change could pass these tests unnoticed.

PINNED SERDE PATH AND THE 128-CONTAINER GUARD. The custody supplied is serde/serde_core/serde_derive 1.0.229 in bodies/SERDE_LOCK-1 through SERDE_LOCK-3 and serde_json 1.0.151, checksum c841b55ecdae098c80dcae9cf767f6f8a0c2cdb3416bbef72181df4d0fe73f14, in SERDE_LOCK-4. bodies/SERDE_SOURCE_CUSTODY/SOURCE-CUSTODY.json and SERDE_SOURCE_ARCHIVE_CUSTODY state de.rs, read.rs, error.rs, map.rs, number.rs and value/de.rs match the locked archive; macros.rs, value/mod.rs, value/ser.rs and value/partial_eq.rs were also supplied. parse_budgeted uses serde_json::Deserializer::from_str, hence StrRead/SliceRead, not IoRead. In SERDE_FULL_DE/de.rs, Deserializer::new sets 'remaining_depth: 128'; check_recursion decrements that allowance when entering an array/object and returns ErrorCode::RecursionLimitExceeded when it reaches zero. It counts nested containers on the current path only, not BudgetSeed value nodes, not object keys and not scalars. The Rustdoc and contract doc statements that 'that deserializer refuses the 128th nested array/object container (recursion limit exceeded) regardless of a larger caller max_depth' are therefore correct under the recorded build, and the warning 'Do not silently clamp caller depth to 32 or 127, and do not disable the callee recursion guard' is the right disposition. The contract's container-versus-value distinction is also correct: a scalar at BudgetSeed depth D follows D enclosing containers, whereas the deepest empty container at depth D is itself container D+1. The documented nested-array example, 127 containers plus scalar succeeding under adequate budgets and 128 containers returning Json 'recursion limit exceeded' rather than Budget Depth, follows from the source. This does not license disabling recursion protection, and caller max_depth larger than the callee container allowance is an upper bound, not acceptance.

NUMBERS RECONCILED. Without arbitrary_precision, SERDE_FULL_DE/de.rs routes unsigned integer significands to U64, negative integers fitting i64 to I64, and significand overflow/decimal/exponent paths to f64 construction. f64_from_parts returns NumberOutOfRange, displayed 'number out of range', when the finite conversion would be infinite. SERDE_FULL_NUMBER/number.rs Number::from_f64 likewise rejects nonfinite values; BudgetSeed::visit_f64's 'nonfinite JSON number' is a defensive guard largely pre-empted on this text path. The coverage assertions for 1.5, -0.25, 0.1, 1e2, 1E-3, 2.5e-1, -1.5e+2, 1e308, 1e-999 underflow to finite 0.0, 0e999, 1e309/-1e309 and a 401-digit integer as 'number out of range', u64::MAX, i64::MAX/MIN, and 18446744073709551616 becoming finite f64 2^64, are source-consistent. Signed zero required and received a representation assertion rather than a runtime-left copy alone: de.rs parse_number(false, 0) expressly computes neg=(0i64).wrapping_neg() and, because 'neg >= 0', returns ParserNumber::F64(-(significand as f64)), i.e. F64(-0.0). The final test unwraps parse_budgeted("-0", BIG), asserts is_f64(), asserts as_f64().map(f64::is_sign_negative)==Some(true), and asserts equality with json!(-0.0). That pins sign; bare f64 equality alone would not distinguish -0.0 from +0.0. This is a test correction, not production normalization, and no new number policy is introduced.

EOF VERSUS PRESENT-INVALID-CHARACTER MEANINGS. The malformed-number correction is independently justified from SERDE_FULL_DE/de.rs rather than by copying observed left-hand strings. parse_decimal, when no fraction digit follows '.', returns EofWhileParsingValue if peek() is None and InvalidNumber if a character is present. parse_exponent returns EofWhileParsingValue when next_char() is None after 'e' or 'e+' and InvalidNumber for a present non-digit. parse_integer after '-' likewise returns EofWhileParsingValue at EOF and InvalidNumber for a present non-digit. The final test therefore correctly changes bare "1.", "1e", "1e+" and "-" to 'EOF while parsing a value' and adds the present-character companions "1.x", "1eX", "1e+X" and "-x" expecting 'invalid number'. '01' remains invalid number and '+1'/'.5'/'NaN'/'Infinity' remain 'expected value', while '0x10' parses root 0 then fails trailing. assert_json_meaning still pins exact code mori::core::json, offset None, step None and the derived substring, so this is not weakening to any-error.

UNICODE, STRINGS AND DECODED KEYS. SERDE_FULL_READ/read.rs on the validate=true String path decodes a valid surrogate pair to its supplementary code point, rejects a trailing surrogate with 'lone leading surrogate in hex escape', rejects an unpaired leading surrogate with 'unexpected end of hex escape' or the corresponding lone-leading error when a non-trailing code unit follows, rejects invalid hex/escapes with 'invalid escape', and rejects raw U+0000-U+001F with 'control character (\\u0000-\\u001F) found while parsing a string'. No Unicode normalization is performed. The final coverage correctly asserts U+1F600 from \\uD83D\\uDE00, BMP escapes, the escape-heavy string in the previously passing unicode function preserved byte-exact, lone/unpaired surrogate refusals, invalid escapes, raw control characters, precomposed U+00E9 distinct from e+U+0301 as both values and keys, escaped/literal decoded-key duplication before the duplicate value, and sibling-object keys not colliding. The rejected owner whole-after file in bodies/REJECTED_WHOLE_AFTER/OWNER-WHOLE-AFTER-NOT-SELECTED.rs, which removed one quote on the Unicode line, was not adopted; bodies/CONTRADICTORY_WHOLE_AFTER_DIFF/OWNER-WHOLE-AFTER-CONTRADICTION.diff proves the selected 14325-byte literal-only source preserved that quote. The lifetime change itself is proved by bodies/SELECTED_LIFETIME_ONLY_DIFF/SELECTED-LIFETIME-ONLY.diff and LITERAL_INTAKE_PROOF: only 'let binding = nested_arrays(33);' plus borrowing &binding was applied to the original 14298-byte coverage preimage, producing 14325 bytes SHA256 8d6fc9f2fb50e825cf49a95013a79199d775ea838b2820dd6b4261abb7367ae2.

LEGACY, EXPORT AND INDIRECT-COVERAGE LIMITS. Comparing bodies/BEFORE_JSON/json.rs (5391 bytes) with C07 and the Rustdoc after-file shows legacy Seed still uses depth > 32 or nodes > 65_536, MAX_BYTES remains 1_048_576, parse still uses 'JSON exceeds 1 MiB', parse_limited retains its caller ceiling/message, deserialize_strict starts Seed at depth 0 with a fresh Cell, and export still pretty-serializes, reparses, escapes non-ASCII/control characters as UTF-16 units, checks escaped length and reparses. The new eleven functions directly exercise legacy parse depth 32/33, nodes 65_536/65_537 through flat arrays, exact 1 MiB and one-over byte text, parse_limited ceiling/message and legacy depth, and deserialize_strict duplicate, ordinary and depth-33 paths. They do not runtime-test export at all in the final eleven functions; export correctness rests on source comparison and the contract statement, not on the recorded final runtime. deserialize_strict node-boundary through a non-text deserializer and callers' responsibility to perform any trailing end() check after deserialize_strict are only indirectly covered; the function itself performs no trailing check, and the document's phrase 'none of its own' for its byte bound should be read in that caller-composed sense. The internal json.rs unit test duplicate_decoded_keys_and_trailing_data_reject is in production source but was not one of the eleven external final functions or the old three external functions.

SOURCE-INFORMED EXPECTATIONS AND ORACLE LIMITS. The new tests construct expected Values with serde_json json!, Value constructors and accessors from the same pinned serde_json library used by the parser. json! scalar interpolation routes through to_value/value::Serializer per SERDE_ADDITIONAL_macros_rs/macros.rs, SERDE_ADDITIONAL_value_ser_rs/ser.rs and value/mod.rs. This same-library coupling means Value/Number construction and equality are source-exposed conditional parser/library expectations, not a source-blind financial oracle and not independent evidence of what an external JSON implementation would produce. The pre-consumer independent counts are stronger for byte/node/depth of the old valid witnesses but still only ordinary Python UTF-8/JSON tree counting. No universal compiler, Std, OS, allocator, loader or exhaustive-input proof is supplied; I do not substitute that unrelated universal goal for a concrete CoreJSON finding, and I do not claim one.

REMAINING CONCRETE GAPS, NOT HIDDEN FAILURES. First, exact serde_json line/column suffixes and complete Json messages are not golden-tested, as stated above. Second, the recursion tests witness scalar-deepest nested arrays at 127/128 containers and alternating containers only to depth 3; there is no separate deepest-empty-container witness, such as nested empty arrays where the deepest container is container D+1, no 128-deep object-only chain, and no object-heavy wide counterpart to flat_array(1000). Third, export is untested by the recorded final runtime. Fourth, old witness valueNodes/maxDepth metadata are present but, in the old three-function file, only indirectly exercised for some witnesses. Fifth, the recorded build is conditional on the supplied fingerprint features default/std with unbounded_depth, arbitrary_precision and preserve_order not enabled for this build; downstream feature unification enabling those features can change recursion, Number or Map behaviour and is outside the contract, as the document expressly states. Sixth, no caller-selected production budgets, service retry policy or resource-adequacy decision is supplied; budget values are caller upper bounds, not a denial-of-service theorem. None of these is a demonstrated defect in the audited depth 0-127 container, budget, duplicate, number, Unicode or legacy boundary predicates, and none justifies disabling the recursion guard, clamping caller depth to 32/127, or transferring backend clamps into Core. They must not, however, be described as closed by the eleven test names.

COMPILER, NORMAL CORE AND EFFECT QUALIFICATIONS. The final build reuses pinned current external Core 4add..., whose lib.rs differs from the older library by an additive R1 source-bounds module while the JSON source f615 remains identical; historical metadata mentioning older C paths does not establish live C equality after R1 integration, and no Core rebuild of the Rustdoc-only after-file was claimed. The complete 92-source map/cohort/tool/hash inventories are marked WHOLE AVAILABLE with explicit non-read status; their paths and hashes do not show I read all third-party source and do not establish a universal trusted-computing-base theorem. If a CoreJSON claim required a dependency not actually supplied as a mandatory body, it would have to be qualified; for the concrete counting, number, string, error, recursion and Map/Value predicates decided here, the supplied locked serde_json de/read/error/map/number/value sources are sufficient source evidence. The tested functions construct in-memory strings and Values and invoke public Core JSON plus serde from_str/Value/json! paths; they perform no SDK, VM, proof, ledger, key or network operation at test level, and target/host dependency-directory presence is not proof every dependency row loaded or every proc macro executed. Static call-path inspection and ordinary host build/test observations do not prove OS/network containment, compiler/allocator/libtest/loader correctness or service resource adequacy.

DECISION. Subject to the explicit qualifications above, the proposed Rustdoc and contract document do not misstate parse_budgeted, parse, parse_limited, deserialize_strict or export on the supplied source; the final eleven-function coverage corrects four malformed positives while retaining them as trailing negatives, retains duplicate/Depth streaming precedences, pins signed-zero representation and EOF-versus-invalid-character meanings from source, preserves all previously passing bodies, and matches root's recorded 11 PASS result. Historical backend canonical clamps, Fields/TryFrom and V1-V13 remain context only and are not approved. Decision: approve-source-only for this proposed CoreJSON source consideration. Root alone may integrate the six files and decide any later adoption; full parent/backend R4 V1-V13, compiler correctness, ACTUS/financial conformance, native/SDK/proof/ledger/EARS acceptance and security/runtime adoption remain open.
